objective: Prove that when every ring of a running network of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts splits into a 2 x 2 block at every lag (every contact cut and both halves born), no cell ever depends on another ring's first row through a contact, so no contact needs a ring it does not touch and no ring hears another; and compute, with doubling every P lags (P = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8) from the 3 x 3 and 4 x 4 tubes, how far each original ring's first row reaches in the original lattice's units, against the frozen horizon expectation, and how the balls of rings a contact needs grow.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (by hand; finite claims checked exactly; the horizon computed; pre-registered): with doubling at every lag no ring ever hears another (every contact is reborn before any cell reads it), so the doubling network reads no distance while it grows; with doubling every P lags (P = 2 to 8) an original ring's reach stays below 0.8 to 2.4 original spacings and only the original rings inside it hear it (none for P <= 4), the same on 3 x 3 and 5 x 5: a horizon.
title: While it doubles every lag, no ring hears another
